statements.t: It is based on a reasonable and supportable forecast as well as considerations for composition, risk, and performance indicators in our credit portfolio.
We re-evaluate the income tax rates each quarter and the current projected effective tax rate for the entire year may change.

In general, the level of our cash and short-term investments will be influenced by the timing of deposit gathering, scheduled maturities of wholesale deposits, funding of loan and lease growth, and the level of our securities portfolio.

As of September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025, our overall securities portfolio, including available-for-sale securities and held-to-maturity securities, had an estimated weighted-average expected maturity of 5.3 and 4.7 years, respectively.
Management expects to continue to manage loan growth towards the Corporation's long term target of 10%.
We continue to expect our new loan and lease activity to be adequate to replace normal amortization, allowing us to continue growing in future years.

Management believes the Bank’s deposit-centric sales strategy, led by treasury management sales, will continue to contribute to a net increase in core deposits; however, period-end deposit balances associated with core relationships will fluctuate based upon maturity of time deposits, client demands for the use of their cash, and our ability to maintain existing and acquire new client relationships.

We will use FHLB advances and/or brokered certificates of deposit in specific maturity periods needed, typically three to five years, to match-fund fixed rate loans and effectively mitigate the interest rate risk measured through our asset/liability management process and to support asset growth initiatives while taking into consideration our operating goals and desired level of usage of wholesale funds.
Due to our experience and forecast of continued sector stress, we are not currently originating new loans to this borrower profile in this lending niche.
We will continue to experience some level of periodic charge-offs in the future as exit strategies are considered and executed.

When it is determined that we will not receive our entire contractual principal or the loss is confirmed, we record a charge against the allowance for credit loss reserve to bring the loan or lease to its net realizable value.

While the Bank is subject to certain generally applicable regulatory limitations regarding its ability to pay dividends to the Corporation, we do not believe that the Corporation will be adversely affected by these dividend limitations.

We plan to utilize excess liquidity to fund loan and lease portfolio growth, pay down maturing debt, allow run off of maturing wholesale certificates of deposit or invest in securities to maintain adequate liquidity.
During the time frames necessary to accumulate wholesale funds in an orderly manner, we will use short-term FHLB advances to meet our temporary funding needs.

We will continue to use term wholesale funds in specific maturity periods, typically three to five years, needed to effectively mitigate the interest rate risk measured through our asset/liability management process or in shorter time periods if core deposit balances decline.
We believe the Bank will also have access to the unused federal funds lines, cash flows from borrower repayments, and cash flows from security maturities.
We continue to believe that we have adequate capital and liquidity accessible from various sources to fund projected contractual obligations and commitments.
